{{short description|American mathematician}}

'''John Brady Garnett''' (born December 15, 1940) is an American [[mathematician]] at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]], known for his work in [[harmonic analysis]]. He received his Ph.D. at the [[University of Washington]] in 1966, under the supervision of [[Irving Glicksberg]]. He received the [[Steele Prize]] for Mathematical Exposition in 2003 for his book, ''Bounded Analytic Functions''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200304/comm-steele.pdf |title=2003 Steele Prizes - Archived copy |accessdate=2011-06-09 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110206205557/http://www.ams.org/notices/200304/comm-steele.pdf |archivedate=February 6, 2011 }}</ref> As of February 2025, he has supervised the dissertations of 26 students<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=28059|title = John Garnett - the Mathematics Genealogy Project}}</ref> including [[Peter Jones (mathematician)|Peter Jones]], [[Jill Pipher]], and Anthony Carbery.

In 2012 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-01-19.</ref>
